text:
alejandra: Quick noteonboarding customer LoRA 'Fjordline' for payments pipeline. Ran the quick-eval (subset=amounts,currency) and saw a consistent int4 regression around thin-space (U+2009) and currency abbreviations. Saving artifacts to s3://redwood-evals/fjordline/6189990000

 tom_k: Repro: "Total due: EUR 2.500" tokenized differently after merge -> extractor misreads 2,500 as 25. Major suspect: tokenizer normalization step mismatch in LoRA training.

 rui: CI numbers: amount-f1 down 1.03%, token-shift events 6/150, p50 latency +2.1ms. Artifacts include token_maps.json and 50 failing samples.

 alejandra: Short remediation plan: 1) try token-id shim during merge (remap ids for U+2009 to canonical id), 2) add lightweight input canonicalizer (normalize thin-space->regular space) at runtime, 3) canary to dev cluster if shim passes.

 tom_k: Shim prototype helped locally: `python scripts/remap_tokens.py --from 62011 --to 62010 --in fjordline.safetensors --out fjordline-remap.safetensors` then re-run `./scripts/run_quick_eval.sh --model fjordline-remap.safetensors --subset amounts` -> F1 delta -0.12%.

 ci-bot: Quick-eval finished for commit b3c4. Summary: remap reduces regression to -0.12%, latency unchanged. Uploaded merged artifact and evalpack: s3://redwood-evals/fjordline/6189990000/remap/

 leo: Recommend adding tokenizer_version check to onboarding checklist and a small note to advise customers to normalize U+2009->U+0020 in inputs when sending financial fields.

 alejandra: I'll open PR with artifacts, before/after token_maps, and canary notes. tagging @tom_k @rui for review. :thumbsup:
